newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sour crudes weaken late on higher supplies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sour crudes weaken late on higher supplies.

text.p: U.S. sour crudes weakened late Wednesday dampened by rising supplies from Latin America and upcoming sales from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR).

"Re-affirmation of the SPR sale brought sour prices down, and potential buyers are also holding out," an East Coast trader said, expecting West Texas Sour to hit the skids and recede to a more typical spread against WTI soon.
November West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $24.00-10 a barrel, down 30 cents from Tuesday.
The Nov/Dec WTI spread narrowed 10-15 cents to 95 cents, further restricting Brent-related crude sales to the U.S.
Activity was moderate, with some refiners homing in on Louisiana barrels spurred on by the narrowing European import arbitrage, but demand tapered off later in the session.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded briskly between WTI plus 42 and 38 cents, recovering later to 40 cents.
Midland/WTI was thin but some said a handful of trades were done at plus 4 and 6 cents over the U.S. benchmark. And Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was dealt at 20 cts premium.
Sours were weaker, hurt by perception of rising supplies amid a seasonal preference for lighter grades, traders said.
West Texas Sour/Midland traded at minus $1.28-$1.25.
The grade has lost about four cents from Tuesday, before the government approved further sales from the SPR.
Eugene Island saw trades between $1.08-$1.10 below the WTI, steady from talk on Tuesday.
But WTI/Cushing Postings Plus drifted lower, partly due to the flatter backwardation, at 47 cents compared with 58 cents earlier Wednesday.
